page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v6 is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 128 virtual CPUs and 512 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating on the x86_64 architecture with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. Dedicated compute capacity is divided across 64 physical cores using two threads per core. The processor subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, Intel AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, alongside hardware cryptography capabilities.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute and data handling capabilities. In multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench workloads, the instance achieves top-quartile execution scores, driven by the massive core volume and large shared cache. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 702.64 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations and Redis SET throughput place the server in the top ten percent of evaluated systems. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 508.63 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including single-core stress-ng and compression operations, register in the median tier, indicating that per-thread frequency gains are secondary to parallel scalability.

The D128s_v6 provides no integrated local disk storage and zero hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures with Premium Storage support. This stateless disk design prevents ephemeral data loss on host migration but requires external network storage provisioning for persistent state. CPU-based machine learning inference benchmark results show strong performance for prompt processing across model sizes, supported by AMX acceleration. The server fits high-concurrency enterprise workloads including distributed relational databases, in-memory key-value caches, multi-threaded software compilation pipelines, and large-scale web serving tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D128s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8573C processors. It provides 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 512 GB, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, while containing no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs. In benchmarks, the server demonstrates exceptional multi-threaded performance, recording top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and high-volume Redis transactions. While single-threaded throughput falls within average bands, aggregate throughput and large-block memory read bandwidth remain exceptionally high. The architecture is well matched for horizontally threaded enterprise workloads, including large database servers, compilation pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, and multi-core CPU inference tasks.
